messages:
joanne: Quick kickoff — proposal to standardize our internal API surface as a capability-first graph, not just RPCs. Idea: define capabilities (e.g. embeddings, rerank, snippet-generation) with stable semantic contracts, then map them to transport-specific bindings (gRPC/proto for internal, JSON-over-HTTP for edge). Thoughts?

mike: I like capability-first. Means clients talk about intent not transport. +1 for stable semantics so we can swap implementations without client churn.

zheng: Curious about versioning here. If capability semantics evolve, how do we present compat guarantees? Major/minor capability versions?

joanne: Yes — propose capability version in the capability descriptor: e.g. capability_id: text-embed:v1.1. Backwards compatibility rules: semver-like for behaviour. Transport adapters must surface capability_version.

mike: Also need routing policy implications. If we route by capability, we can send traffic to different model backends per capability-version. But quotas and billing are usually tied to service & route today. We should decide mapping between capability, tenant quota buckets, and cost labels.

darren: Big ops ask: telemetry and dashboards. We need per-capability latency/p99, token-cost, error-rate. If we hide transport behind adapters, ensure adapters emit normalized spans and metric labels: capability_id, capability_version, backend_model, region, tenant_id.

zheng: +1 for normalized labels. Also request: include a route-tag header so rollout UX can target a subset of tenants. Something like X-Redwood-Route-Tag: canary-42.

joanne: Exactly. Rollout UX: console should let PMs pick capability + version + route-tag to create canaries. We need enforcement points: gateway should attach route-tag and quota middleware should evaluate per (tenant, capability, tag).

infra-bot: deploybot: canary job created for capability text-embed:v1.1 -> backend pool embed-pool-12; notify @darren for telemetry hook up.

mike: Back to transports — do we mandate a single proto descriptor for each capability and then generate both gRPC and REST/JSON stubs from it? Pros: single source of truth. Cons: sometimes JSON ergonomics differ.

zheng: We could make proto canonical but allow optional transport-specific adapters (e.g., simplified JSON wrapper with examples) in the developer docs. Adapter projects live as small translation layers in the gateway repo.

darren: One operational concern: prefixes and caching. If capabilities accept variable prompt shapes, cache keys must include capability_version + normalized input fingerprint. We'll need a standard canonicalization util published in SDKs.

joanne: Good call. I'll sketch an initial spec: capability manifest fields (id, version, schema, semantics, cost_unit, routing_hints, telemetry_labels). Gateway runtime uses manifest to wire routing, quota, and telemetry. SDKs implement canonicalization + route-tag helpers.

mike: Example manifest snippet would help.

joanne: put this in thread — quick proto-ish example:```proto
// capability manifest (pseudo)
message CapabilityManifest {
  string id = 1; // e.g. "text-embed"
  string version = 2; // "v1.1"
  string schema_uri = 3; // link to JSON schema
  repeated string routing_hints = 4; // low-latency, cost-sensitive
  string cost_unit = 5; // token or request
}
```

zheng: That looks fine. One more: quotas. We must support hard quotas (enforced at gateway) and soft budget alerts (console). Hard quota keys: (tenant_id, capability_id, capability_version, route_tag).

darren: For telemetry, will the gateway emit an enriched span for each request? We need trace IDs preserved to link to backend model traces. If we do distributed tracing, attach the capability metadata as tags/attributes.

joanne: Agreed. Also propose a migration plan: start with a single capability (text-embed) and implement proto manifest + gateway adapter + console canary flow. Use it as prototype before broad rollout.

mike: timeline?

joanne: Proposed: week 1 spec + manifest proto; week 2 gateway adapter + metric labels; week 3 console canary UI + quota middleware; week 4 internal dogfood.

zheng: I'll volunteer to own the gateway adapter for embed. darren can you own telemetry hooks?

darren: Yes, will wire metrics and traces. Also will add sample dashboards: per-capability p50/p95/p99, cost per unit, error budget.

joanne: sweet. I'll author a short RFC doc and link it here when ready. Thanks all. :rocket:
